_comment: Which hooks under hooks/ are wired live into ~/.claude/settings.json, and to which event surface. check-judge-listed.py (SPEC INV-211, gate v) reds when a wired judge is absent from its surface's hook array — the no-verdict failure of a judge whose file is present but whose settings.json entry is gone. A library hook is one the pack does not wire into its default settings.json — a hook invoked by another hook (register_judge_core), a shipped file a hook reads at runtime beside its own (turn_reader.py, the shared turn reader every Stop-side scan judges through), or an OPT-IN hook a host turns on by adding it to their own settings.json (the conduct-judge arms, the lean-orchestrator-scan net); gate v never demands a library hook be live, so an opt-in net keeps the suite green until a host enables it. Every file under hooks/ must appear in exactly one of the two lists, or the gate reds asking that it be classified — the self-widening honesty config-health (gate m) already uses.
_installer_fields_comment: ROADMAP row 506: 'file'/'command'/'matcher'/'data'/'personal_overlay' let the setup walk GENERATE its coverage from this declaration instead of hand-keeping a second list that drifts. 'file' is the repo hooks/ basename (the wired key carries no extension). 'command' is the plain invocation form this host's ~/.claude/settings.json actually carries today (read 2026-07-27) — for a hook this host also wraps in the personal, unshipped counter ~/.claude/hooks/hook-meter.py, 'command' still states the PLAIN form, since hook-meter.py is the personal layer's own instrument (its docstring says so) and is never installed or assumed by the pack; an installer detects a hook already wired in ANY form (plain or meter-wrapped) by the hook's filename appearing in the existing command string, so a host's own meter-wrapped entry is left exactly as it stands, never re-written to the plain form. 'matcher' names the PreToolUse/Stop matcher the entry carries in settings.json today, null where none (every one of the eight today). 'data' lists the shipped hooks/ files a hook reads at runtime beside its own file (turn_reader.py, register_judge_core.py, register-judge.py), installed alongside it. 'personal_overlay' names the optional per-hook file pattern that lives ONLY on a host's machine (never shipped, never created or overwritten by an installer, reported by name when present) — this is distinct from hook-meter.py, which is a cross-cutting personal wrapper rather than one hook's own overlay.
